To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the optimal solution of the assignment problem is obtained by solving a corresponding occupancy problem and (2) the optimal solution to the occupancy problem is obtained by finding a solution to a corresponding assignment problem.
the optimal assignment for the expected completion time problem is obtained by sorting records by the number of records assigned to a device and assigning records to devices in the sorted order.

(1) the optimal solution of the record-to-device assignment problem is obtained by solving the occupancy problem with the expected number of requests per record, the expected number of records per device, and the expected number of devices per request as parameters, (2) an optimal solution of the block-to-record assignment problem is obtained using the same occupancy problem as a parameter, and (3), the performance of the hashing scheme is analyzed in terms of the occupancy problem parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problems: (1) the problem of assigning records to devices, (2), the problem of assigning blocks to records, and

the following problems: (1) The optimal assignment of records to secondary memory blocks, (2) The optimal assignment and scheduling of jobs to devices, (3) The optimal assignment to buckets of records whose record-to-bucket probabilities are different, (4) The analysis of a hashing scheme in which the record-to-buckets probabilities are not the same.
the following problems: (a) the optimal assignment of records to blocks in secondary memory, and (b) the performance of a hash file under non-uniform record-to-bucket probabilities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimal solution is obtained by solving a related occupancy problem.
the optimal placement of the records is obtained by assigning the most frequent records to the most frequent devices and by assigning the least frequent records to the least frequent devices.
, if the record-to-buckets probability is uniform, the optimal assignment of records to buckets is to assign each bucket the records in a random permutation of the records.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expected number of records assigned to the device is the same as the expected number of blocks to access.
we have shown how to assign records to blocks so that the expected completion time is minimum.

, for the first problem, the optimal solution is given by a greedy algorithm; for the second problem, the optimal allocation of records to blocks is achieved when the number of records in each block is the same; for the third problem, an optimal allocation of records is achieved when the record-to-buckets probability is uniform.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal solution for one problem is not necessarily optimal for another.
, when the record-to-buckets probability is not uniform, a hashing scheme with a large number of buckets can perform worse than one with a smaller number of buckets.
the performance of a system can be significantly improved by using a good record-to-device, page, or bucket assignment.
